title: A Better Understanding of Long Covid

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Throughout the pandemic, long COVID has remained something of a medical mystery.
sentences.zh: 在整个大流行期间，“长期新冠”一直是某种医学谜团。

sentences.en: Now, amid the latest surge of infections, a series of major studies are shedding new light on who is getting long COVID and just how widespread the condition actually is.
sentences.zh: 如今，在最新一波感染潮中，一系列重大研究为“究竟是谁在感染长期新冠”以及“这种病症究竟有多普遍”提供了新的见解。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Pam Bellick, about what we're learning.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事帕姆·贝利克就我们的新发现进行了交谈。

sentences.en: It's Friday, May 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月20日，星期五。

sentences.en: Pam, you have been reporting on long COVID since the term first emerged.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，自从这个词出现以来，你一直在报道长期新冠。

sentences.en: And for the longest time, our understanding of it has been highly anecdotal.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来，我们对它的理解基本上都停留在传闻阶段。

sentences.en: We have mentioned it several times on the show, and we know that lots of people are very worried about it, but we've never had that much real data about long COVID.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中多次提到过它，我们也知道很多人对此非常担心，但我们从来没有关于长期新冠的那么多真实数据。

sentences.en: And that seems to have now changed, right?
sentences.zh: 现在情况似乎变了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What we've been seeing in the past few months is studies that are looking at very, very large amounts of data, usually from medical records.
sentences.zh: 过去几个月我们看到的是，研究人员正在研究非常非常庞大的数据量，通常来自医疗记录。

sentences.en: And we've had enough time now, you know, the pandemic has gone on, obviously, for more than two years.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有足够的时间了，你知道的，大流行显然已经持续了两年多。

sentences.en: And so we have had enough time now to be able to look at questions like how many people seem to be suffering, what kind of symptoms they have, how long it's going on,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们现在有足够的时间来研究诸如“有多少人似乎在受苦”、“他们有什么症状”、“这种情况持续了多久”之类的问题，

sentences.en: who's at risk, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 谁处于危险之中，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So we are getting a high-level picture that helps us kind of color in between the lines a little bit and giving us a better sense of what this condition is like.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们正在获得一个宏观的图景，这有助于我们把细节描绘得更清楚一点，让我们对这种病症有更好的了解。

sentences.en: And just to begin with, how do these studies define long COVID?
sentences.zh: 首先，这些研究是如何定义长期新冠的？

sentences.en: Because the phrase itself has always felt pretty ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 因为这个短语本身一直让人感觉相当含糊。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that definition still isn't entirely clear.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这个定义仍然不是很清楚。

sentences.en: Basically, the general definition is symptoms that occur after the initial COVID infection that people have had.
sentences.zh: 基本上，通用的定义是人们在初次感染新冠后出现的症状。

sentences.en: some places like the CDC start the clock a month or more after.
sentences.zh: 有些地方，比如美国疾病控制与预防中心，将时间点定在一个月或更久之后。

sentences.en: So if you're still experiencing symptoms or you're experiencing new symptoms a month or more after you've had COVID, then you could be considered to have long COVID.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在感染新冠一个月或更久之后仍然经历着症状，或者出现新的症状，那么你就可以被认为患有长期新冠。

sentences.en: The World Health Organization defines it starting at three months later.
sentences.zh: 世界卫生组织将其定义为三个月后开始。

sentences.en: But basically, the simplest definition is if you're experiencing symptoms that are lasting weeks or months or emerging weeks or months later, that qualifies as long COVID.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，最简单的定义是，如果你正在经历持续数周或数月、或者在数周或数月后出现的症状，这就符合长期新冠的标准。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So symptoms that are occurring at least a month after an original infection and cannot really be explained by anything else.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在初次感染至少一个月后出现且无法用其他原因解释的症状。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And that's a really important point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的点。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And what are those symptoms according to these studies?
sentences.zh: 根据这些研究，这些症状是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the symptoms can really run the gamut and they can affect every part of the body, every organ system.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些症状可以说是包罗万象，它们会影响身体的各个部位、各个器官系统。

sentences.en: Everything from trouble breathing, coughing, gastrointestinal symptoms, problems with heartbeat issues and rapid heartbeat and dizziness and that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 从呼吸困难、咳嗽、胃肠道症状，到心跳问题、心跳过速以及头晕等各种情况。

sentences.en: Fatigue is really, really common.
sentences.zh: 疲劳真的非常非常普遍。

sentences.en: People just feeling so tired and unable to get back to their normal energy level.
sentences.zh: 人们只是感到非常疲惫，无法恢复到正常的精力水平。

sentences.en: And then when they try, they can have setbacks.
sentences.zh: 然后当他们试图恢复时，病情可能会反复。

sentences.en: There are a whole bunch of brain-related or cognitive issues that people are experiencing.
sentences.zh: 人们正在经历一堆与大脑相关或认知方面的问题。

sentences.en: You've probably heard the term brain fog.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过“脑雾”这个词。

sentences.en: Sometimes that's sort of a catch-all term that's used for things like not remembering things, not being able to concentrate, not being able to pay attention the way you used to.
sentences.zh: 有时这是一个笼统的词，用来指代诸如记不住事情、无法集中注意力、无法像以前那样保持专注等情况。

sentences.en: So pretty much anything that you can think of that your body does or that your brain does can become a symptom depending on the person.
sentences.zh: 因此，几乎任何你能想到的你身体或大脑能做的事情，因人而异都可能成为一种症状。

sentences.en: It's an extraordinarily wide range of symptoms from one virus.
sentences.zh: 由一种病毒引起的症状范围之广令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very nebulous at this point.
sentences.zh: 是的，目前它非常模糊。

sentences.en: And I think that's part of the reason that doctors and scientists are having trouble kind of pinpointing a definition.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是医生和科学家们难以确切给出一个定义的部分原因。

sentences.en: The other reason is that we don't really know what the underlying cause or causes are.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是我们真的不知道其根本原因是什么。

sentences.en: And so I actually think that as we learn more, it may be likely that there end up being, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我实际上认为，随着我们了解的更多，最终很可能会出现，你知道的，

sentences.en: three or four different flavors of long COVID that have different causes and that have a different set of symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 三四种不同类型的长期新冠，它们有不同的成因和一组不同的症状。

sentences.en: But right now, we're still really very much in the discovery phase and the reporting phase.
sentences.zh: 但现在，我们确实仍处于发现阶段和报告阶段。

sentences.en: And so that's why people have had this sort of huge basket of, you know, something like 200 symptoms that different people have reported.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们会有这样一大堆，你知道的，大约200种不同的人报告过的症状。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: What you just said feels important.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说的话感觉很重要。

sentences.en: even though we have these major surveys that track thousands and thousands of people who have
sentences.zh: 尽管我们有这些追踪了成千上万患有

sentences.en: long COVID, you're saying we're not that much closer to understanding why COVID-19 causes these long-term varied symptoMs. Right.
sentences.zh: 长期新冠的患者的大型调查，但你说我们对“为什么新冠肺炎会导致这些长期的、各种各样的症状”并没有更深入的理解。没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, we're getting little hints that it might be related, for example, to the surge of inflammation that we know the virus causes when people first get infected.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们得到了一些小线索，表明它可能与病毒在人们刚感染时引发的炎症激增有关。

sentences.en: Some people get kind of a huge surge of inflammation.
sentences.zh: 有些人会产生某种巨大的炎症激增。

sentences.en: And so inflammation can cause all sorts of bad things in the body.
sentences.zh: 因此，炎症会在体内引起各种各样糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: And it's possible that people who experience long
sentences.zh: 而且经历长期新冠的人

sentences.en: COVID have either ongoing damage from that inflammatory reaction, or they're continuing to have inflammation that's causing damage.
sentences.zh: 可能要么还在承受那种炎症反应带来的持续损害，要么他们的炎症仍在继续并造成损害。

sentences.en: That's one theory.
sentences.zh: 这是一种理论。

sentences.en: Another theory has to do with the immune system response.
sentences.zh: 另一种理论与免疫系统反应有关。

sentences.en: And these two things could be sort of related that for people who are experiencing it, their immune system just did not get the memo to shut down.
sentences.zh: 这两者可能是某种程度上相关的，对于正在经历这种情况的人来说，他们的免疫系统只是没有接收到关闭的指令。

sentences.en: Some people think that there may be little fragments of viral genetic material or even little fragments of the virus itself that are kind of hanging around.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为，可能有一些病毒遗传物质的小片段，甚至病毒本身的小片段还在四处游荡。

sentences.en: And they're sort of sending the immune system the signal to keep being activated when really there's just not that much for it to do.
sentences.zh: 它们在某种程度上向免疫系统发送信号，让其保持激活状态，而实际上并没有那么多事情需要它去做。

sentences.en: And so that's another theory.
sentences.zh: 所以这是另一种理论。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So the best working theory we have so far for the cause of long COVID is that COVID itself triggers the body's protections to go into some form of overdrive and stay in overdrive
sentences.zh: 因此，到目前为止，关于长期新冠成因的最佳实用理论是，新冠病毒本身会触发身体的保护机制进入某种过度驱动状态，并保持在过度驱动状态

sentences.en: even when the threat of COVID has subsided.
sentences.zh: 即使新冠病毒的威胁已经消退。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's a leading theory.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个主流理论。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And Pam, what can we say about how many people seem to be experiencing these symptoms after a COVID infection?
sentences.zh: 帕姆，关于有多少人在感染新冠后似乎正在经历这些症状，我们能说些什么？

sentences.en: So, again, one of those questions that has a very wide-ranging answer.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，这是一个答案范围非常广泛的问题。

sentences.en: The best estimates that I've seen from, I guess, several different studies range from about 10% to about 30% of adults.
sentences.zh: 我从大约几项不同的研究所看到的最佳估计是，大约10%到30%的成年人。

sentences.en: You know, it's a very wide range.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这个范围非常广。

sentences.en: The Government Accountability Office just came out with a report a month or so ago.
sentences.zh: 美国政府问责局在一个多月前刚刚发布了一份报告。

sentences.en: And I think they said that as of March, they were estimating that there could be between 7.7 million and 23 million Americans who had long COVID at that point.
sentences.zh: 我想他们说过，截至3月，他们估计当时全美可能有770万到2300万美国人患有长期新冠。

sentences.en: A lot of people.
sentences.zh: 很多人。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it really is a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这确实很多。

sentences.en: I mean, if you think about cancer, the government figures are that 1.6 million people in the United States a year are diagnosed with cancer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想想癌症，政府的数据是美国每年有160万人被诊断出患有癌症。

sentences.en: This is a lot more than 1.6 million.
sentences.zh: 这个数字远超160万。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, it's the size of a major city, you know, or two or three major cities, depending on whether you're picking the upper range of that 23 million figure.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这相当于一个大城市的规模，你知道的，或者是两三个大城市，这取决于你是否选择2300万这个数字的上限。

sentences.en: So it's an awful lot of people.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常庞大的人群。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: On the other hand, 70 to 90 percent of us who get COVID, and at this point, I think we can say us because almost everyone we know has gotten COVID, don't experience long COVID,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，感染新冠的我们当中有70%到90%的人——此时此刻，我想我们可以说“我们”，因为我们认识的几乎所有人都得过新冠——并没有经历长期新冠，

sentences.en: which is the vast majority of people who get infected.
sentences.zh: 这占了感染人数的绝大多数。

sentences.en: That is a more optimistic way of looking at it for sure.
sentences.zh: 从积极的角度来看，这当然是一种更乐观的看法。

sentences.en: Trying.
sentences.zh: 正在努力保持乐观。

sentences.en: And to be clear, what are the surveys telling us, these big studies, about how long these symptoms in long COVID persist?
sentences.zh: 明确一下，这些调查（这些大型研究）告诉我们，长期新冠患者的这些症状会持续多久？

sentences.en: I mean, are they considered indefinite, or do they eventually stop afflicting the people who have long COVID?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们被认为是无限期的，还是最终会停止折磨那些患有长期新冠的人？

sentences.en: Yeah, again, I think it really ranges widely.
sentences.zh: 是的，同样，我认为它的跨度确实非常大。

sentences.en: So we are getting a sense that some people get better just with time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始感觉到有些人仅仅随着时间推移就好了。

sentences.en: So that's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件好事。

sentences.en: but I've certainly talked to many people who have had symptoms last well over a year and sometimes new symptoms kind of emerge
sentences.zh: 但我确实和许多人交谈过，他们的症状持续了一年多，有时新的症状会在

sentences.en: after they think they've conquered a couple of things, something else will happen and I think the other thing to sort of keep in mind here
sentences.zh: 他们以为自己已经战胜了某些问题后出现，其他事情又会发生，我认为这里需要记住的另一件事是

sentences.en: is that for many people this is not a linear recovery process.
sentences.zh: 对于许多人来说，这不是一个线性的康复过程。

sentences.en: It's not like, you know, tomorrow is going to be better than today and then it was better than yesterday.
sentences.zh: 并不是说，你知道的，明天会比今天好，然后又比昨天好。

sentences.en: for a lot of people, especially with things like fatigue, when they sort of exert themselves and
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，特别是在遇到疲劳之类的问题时，当他们付出努力并

sentences.en: think maybe they can get back to the level of activity that they used to have, it will set them back so much that they may have to be lying on the couch for two days.
sentences.zh: 认为自己或许能恢复到过去的活动水平时，病情会严重反复，以至于他们可能不得不连躺两天沙发。

sentences.en: And so it's a very difficult thing for people to kind of plan around and to be able to know, you know, how much they can
sentences.zh: 因此，人们很难围绕这种情况做出计划，也很难知道，你知道的，他们能

sentences.en: take on and how much of their life they can return to, which gets very, very frustrating for people.
sentences.zh: 承担多少，以及他们的生活能恢复多少，这让人们感到非常非常沮丧。

sentences.en: No doubt.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: So now I want to turn to what we are now learning about who is getting long COVID.
sentences.zh: 现在我想转向我们正在了解的关于“谁在感染长期新冠”的内容。

sentences.en: What can you tell us about that?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们说说这方面的情况吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so these studies are really coalescing around a picture of the types of people who are developing long COVID.
sentences.zh: 好的，这些研究确实正在汇聚成一幅关于患上长期新冠的人群特征的图景。

sentences.en: And I think there are five really interesting findings that seem to be pretty solid right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为有五个非常有趣的发现，目前看来相当可靠。

sentences.en: The first finding is that many, many people who had mild or very moderate initial infections with COVID-19 end up getting long COVID.
sentences.zh: 第一个发现是，许多许多初次感染新冠病毒时症状轻微或非常温和的人，最终都患上了长期新冠。

sentences.en: So you do not have to have been hospitalized with your initial infection to end up having lasting, very debilitating symptoms for months.
sentences.zh: 所以你不需要在初次感染时住院，就会最终导致持续数月、非常使人虚弱的症状。

sentences.en: And that is surprising to a lot of people, but several studies have documented this now,
sentences.zh: 这让很多人感到惊讶，但几项研究现在已经记录了这一点，

sentences.en: and one of them that I just reported on looked at 78,000 people who had long COVID and found that more than three-quarters of them had never been hospitalized for their initial infection.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚报道过其中一项研究，它调查了78,000名患有长期新冠的人，发现其中四分之三以上的人在初次感染时从未住院。

sentences.en: That is surprising because I always imagined that a prerequisite for long COVID was pretty meaningful bouts of original COVID.
sentences.zh: 这很让人意外，因为我一直以为患长期新冠的前提是最初得过相当严重的新冠。

sentences.en: Yeah, and certainly people who are hospitalized for COVID have a very high risk of having long-term symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然因新冠住院的人患长期症状的风险非常高。

sentences.en: There's no doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But what is somewhat surprising but very, very true is that the majority of people who are experiencing long COVID never had to be hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 但有些令人惊讶却又千真万确的是，经历长期新冠的大多数人从未住过院。

sentences.en: And that's because the majority of people who have COVID never have to be hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 这是因为感染新冠的大多数人从来都不需要住院。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So bottom line, a garden variety COVID can lead to long COVID, which is another way of saying having a very mild bout doesn't protect you from long COVID.
sentences.zh: 所以总而言之，普通的新冠也能导致长期新冠，换句话说，病情轻微并不能保护你不受长期新冠的影响。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 这是千真万确的。

sentences.en: Even having no symptoms from the initial infection doesn't necessarily protect you.
sentences.zh: 甚至初次感染没有任何症状也不一定能保护你。

sentences.en: I've talked to many people who have been in that category.
sentences.zh: 我跟许多属于这一类的人聊过。

sentences.en: Asymptomatic and still get long COVID.
sentences.zh: 无症状却依然得了长期新冠。

sentences.en: Asymptomatic or basically, you know, just a few days of mild illness and then several weeks later, they can't get off the couch.
sentences.zh: 无症状，或者基本上，你知道的，只是轻微生病几天，然后几周后，他们就起不了沙发了。

sentences.en: What is the second finding?
sentences.zh: 第二个发现是什么？

sentences.en: So the second finding is that many people who have long COVID did have previous health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以第二个发现是，许多患有长期新冠的人确实有先前的健康问题。

sentences.en: You know, things like diabetes, heart problems, autoimmune conditions.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如糖尿病、心脏问题、自身免疫性疾病。

sentences.en: And in one study that I wrote about, you know, about two-thirds of the people had those previous health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 在我写过的一项研究中，你知道的，大约三分之二的人有这些先前的健康问题。

sentences.en: But that means that one-third of people in that big study did not have any previous health condition.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着那项大型研究中三分之一的人没有任何先前的健康状况。

sentences.en: So it is definitely the case that people who were previously very healthy can still get long COVID.
sentences.zh: 所以毫无疑问，以前非常健康的人仍然会得长期新冠。

sentences.en: As one of the people I was talking to said, you know, it's sort of like a roulette wheel.
sentences.zh: 正如我交谈过的一个人所说，你知道的，这有点像轮盘赌。

sentences.en: We really don't know who's going to be more at risk based on what their health was like beforehand.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道根据他们之前的健康状况，谁会面临更高的风险。

sentences.en: So this is yet another way in which long COVID seems to afflict those who might not at all expect to get it because either they had mild COVID or because they're pretty healthy.
sentences.zh: 所以这又是长期新冠似乎会折磨那些完全意想不到会得病的人的另一种方式，因为他们要么新冠症状轻微，要么身体相当健康。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the third finding is kind of also in that unexpected category.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，第三个发现也属于那种意料之外的类别。

sentences.en: And that is that we're seeing a whole lot of people who are younger, basically in kind of the prime of their lives, who are getting long COVID.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们看到有大量更年轻的人，基本上正处于人生黄金时期的人，正在患上长期新冠。

sentences.en: Many studies now are finding that people who are reporting these long-term symptoms are in their 30s, 40s, 50s.
sentences.zh: 现在许多研究发现，报告这些长期症状的人都在30多岁、40多岁、50多岁。

sentences.en: These are people who led very active lives and they are really struggling with long COVID.
sentences.zh: 这些人过着非常活跃的生活，他们现在真的在与长期新冠做斗争。

sentences.en: And we don't really know why that is.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道为什么会这样。

sentences.en: I mean, one theory is that people of that age group, especially active people, they are noticing the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一种理论认为，那个年龄段的人，尤其是活跃的人，他们比那些年龄大得多、

sentences.en: impact of the symptoms more than maybe somebody who is a lot older and already has some health issues, maybe already has some, you know, memory decline.
sentences.zh: 本身就有一些健康问题、可能已经有一些记忆力衰退的人，更能注意到症状的影响。

sentences.en: So it could be that it's just so noticeable that these are the folks who are coming forward and seeking help at clinics and that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以可能只是因为这种影响太明显了，这些人挺身而出，去诊所寻求帮助等等。

sentences.en: But it is definitely a real aspect of the long COVID picture.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对是长期新冠全貌中真实存在的一个方面。

sentences.en: And I've talked to many people who fit into that description.
sentences.zh: 我跟许多符合这种描述的人聊过。

sentences.en: And, you know, just one who I've been following now for several months, a 34-year-old woman named Samantha Lewis in Aurora, Illinois.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，仅仅其中一个我追踪了好几个月的人，是伊利诺伊州奥罗拉市一位34岁的女性，名叫萨曼莎·刘易斯。

sentences.en: She has a very demanding job which she was holding down with no problem before she got COVID and also raising a child with special needs and also doing roller derby.
sentences.zh: 她有一份要求很高且在得新冠前能够轻松胜任的工作，还要抚养一个有特殊需求的孩子，同时还玩轮滑德比。

sentences.en: And she was just very active and a terrific multitasker.
sentences.zh: 她非常活跃，是一个极出色的多任务处理者。

sentences.en: And she had a relatively mild case of COVID.
sentences.zh: 而她当时的COVID病情其实相当轻微。

sentences.en: And several weeks later, she just entered kind of a spiral where she had just many symptoms, fatigue, lots of brain fog.
sentences.zh: 但在几周后，她陷入了一种恶性循环，出现了大量症状：疲劳、严重的脑雾。

sentences.en: She started assigning three employees the same task and not remembering she had done that, not being able to remember how to
sentences.zh: 她开始同时把三项任务分配给三个员工，却不记得自己做过这事，想不起如何

sentences.en: do basic things, tremendous fatigue, had to stop the roller derby, had to stop driving.
sentences.zh: 做那些最基本的事情，伴随着极度的疲劳，不得不放弃轮滑德比，不得不停止开车。

sentences.en: I mean, and all sorts of stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，还有诸如此类的各种状况。

sentences.en: Life-altering symptoms here.
sentences.zh: 这些是会改变人生的症状。

sentences.en: Life-altering symptoms that went on for well over a year.
sentences.zh: 这些会改变人生的症状持续了一年多。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, I've talked to many people with long COVID who have very similar experiences.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我与许多长新冠患者交流过，他们的经历都非常相似。

sentences.en: And, you know, doctors at post-COVID clinics have told me that her situation is really not an extreme case.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，长新冠门诊的医生告诉我，她的情况其实并不算极端。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That makes me wonder, Pam, about kids, the youngest among us.
sentences.zh: 这让我不禁想知道，帕姆，关于孩子们，我们当中最年轻的群体。

sentences.en: Does being under the age of 18 or under the age of 12, does that seem to be any kind of protection against long COVID?
sentences.zh: 18岁以下或12岁以下的年龄，这似乎能对长新冠起到某种保护作用吗？

sentences.en: So we do seem to be finding that kids are at lower risk for this, maybe much lower risk.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发现孩子们患这种病的风险较低，也许风险低得多。

sentences.en: And that's good news, right?
sentences.zh: 这是个好消息，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: However, there certainly are kids.
sentences.zh: 然而，确实也有些孩子。

sentences.en: Most of them seem to be in the preteen or teenage years as opposed to the really young ones.
sentences.zh: 他们大部分似乎处于青春期前或十几岁的年纪，而不是那些真正年幼的孩子。

sentences.en: who are experiencing symptoms like this as well.
sentences.zh: 同样也在经历这样的症状。

sentences.en: And I've talked to several of those kids who, again, were previously sort of healthy, active on the tennis team, on the basketball team, and had relatively mild COVID,
sentences.zh: 我采访过几个这样的孩子，他们同样在之前可以说是很健康的，是网球队、篮球队的活跃分子，COVID病情也相对较轻，

sentences.en: and then weeks later, unable to concentrate in class, unable to play basketball.
sentences.zh: 但几周后，却无法在课堂上集中注意力，无法打篮球。

sentences.en: So it can afflict kids, and there are clinics that have been set up specifically to treat kids with long COVID, but I guess the good news there
sentences.zh: 所以它也会折磨儿童，而且已经设立了专门的诊所来治疗患有长新冠的儿童，但我想那里的好消息是，

sentences.en: is that it does seem to be less of an issue for kids and fewer kids are being affected.
sentences.zh: 对孩子们来说，这似乎不那么成问题，受到影响的孩子也更少。

sentences.en: Okay, and what about the fourth finding about who is getting long COVID?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么关于谁会患上长新冠的第四个发现是什么？

sentences.en: So the fourth finding is that women seem to be at somewhat greater risk for long COVID.
sentences.zh: 第四个发现是，女性患长新冠的风险似乎要高一些。

sentences.en: But we still don't really know if that is because there is a physiological difference, are women just kind of biologically more at risk, which could be possible.
sentences.zh: 但我们仍然不清楚这是因为存在生理差异，还是女性在生物学上确实风险更高，这完全有可能。

sentences.en: Women are more likely to have certain autoimmune diseases, and it's possible that autoimmune conditions increase your risk for something like long
sentences.zh: 女性更有可能患上某些自身免疫性疾病，而自身免疫状况可能会增加你患上类似长

sentences.en: COVID, or they sort of mirror what's going on with long COVID in some ways.
sentences.zh: 新冠的风险，或者它们在某些方面类似于长新冠正在发生的情况。

sentences.en: So there could be a reason why being a woman is going to put you at higher risk.
sentences.zh: 所以，身为女性会让你面临更高风险，这背后可能会有原因。

sentences.en: But it's also possible that women may be more likely to seek help for some of these issues.
sentences.zh: 但也有可能女性更有可能为其中某些问题寻求帮助。

sentences.en: So it's still, you know, not clear why, but we are seeing that maybe 55%, maybe 60% of patients are women.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，原因仍然不太清楚，但我们看到大约55%、甚至60%的患者是女性。

sentences.en: Pam, there really does seem to be a dismal quality to all of these findings about who's getting COVID.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，关于谁会感染COVID的所有这些发现，确实让人感到一种沉重的阴霾。

sentences.en: Because I think it's fair to say that we all want long COVID to be exceedingly rare.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为公平地说，我们都希望长新冠是非常罕见的。

sentences.en: And from these findings, it's not.
sentences.zh: 但从这些发现来看，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Then perhaps we want to think, well, if you're healthy, then you're safe from long COVID.
sentences.zh: 那么我们或许会想，好吧，如果你很健康，那么你就能免受长新冠的影响。

sentences.en: That's not proving true.
sentences.zh: 事实证明并非如此。

sentences.en: And then we want to think, well, if none of those other things are true, we want long COVID to be generally mild and highly manageable.
sentences.zh: 接着我们又会想，好吧，如果上述情况都不成立，我们希望长新冠通常是轻微的且高度可控的。

sentences.en: And in some of the cases you're describing, like this 34-year-old woman, it's not.
sentences.zh: 但在你描述的一些案例中，比如这个34岁的女人，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So this is starting to feel, and I want to be careful with this wording, but it is starting to feel a little bit like a pandemic within a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以这开始让人觉得——我想谨慎使用这个措辞——但它确实开始有点像大流行中的又一场大流行。

sentences.en: People are definitely describing it that way, sort of like a pandemic within a pandemic or a post-pandemic pandemic.
sentences.zh: 人们绝对是这样形容它的，有点像大流行中的大流行，或者后大流行时期的大流行。

sentences.en: And it's affecting a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 它正在影响很多人。

sentences.en: It's going to affect a lot more people.
sentences.zh: 它还将影响更多的人。

sentences.en: So it is a daunting problem for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以这无疑是一个令人生畏的问题。

sentences.en: I think one signal of optimism in, I would say, the fifth finding that's worth noting is that it does seem like vaccines can be helpful in the long COVID picture.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一个乐观的信号，也就是我认为值得注意的第五个发现是，疫苗似乎确实对长新冠的情况有所帮助。

sentences.en: There are a few studies now that suggest that if you're vaccinated and then you get COVID, you're less likely to get long
sentences.zh: 现在有几项研究表明，如果你接种了疫苗然后感染了COVID，你患长

sentences.en: COVID.
sentences.zh: 新冠的可能性就会降低。

sentences.en: But none of these studies are saying that it prevents it altogether.
sentences.zh: 但这些研究都没有说它能完全预防。

sentences.en: It just might reduce your risk.
sentences.zh: 它可能只是降低了你的风险。

sentences.en: And for those who didn't get vaccinated and suddenly get long COVID, do we know anything about what happens when a vaccine is administered afterwards?
sentences.zh: 而对于那些没有接种疫苗却突然患上长新冠的人，我们是否知道事后接种疫苗会发生什么？

sentences.en: Does that do anything to lessen the impacts of long COVID?
sentences.zh: 这会对减轻长新冠的影响起到任何作用吗？

sentences.en: So there have been some surveys of people in that category, and I actually wrote a whole story about this, of people who got COVID before vaccines were available,
sentences.zh: 所以有一些针对该群体人群的调查，实际上我为此写了一整篇报道，关于那些在疫苗问世前感染了COVID、

sentences.en: had terrible brain fog and other types of symptoms, then got vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 患有可怕的脑雾和其他各类症状，后来接种了疫苗的人。

sentences.en: And some of those people, they think 30, 40% maybe of those people did feel better after the vaccination.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人，他们认为大约30%、40%的人在接种疫苗后确实感觉好多了。

sentences.en: But most people didn't really see any difference.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人并没有真正看到任何区别。

sentences.en: And there was a small percentage, like 14, 15% of people who actually said they felt worse after vaccines.
sentences.zh: 还有一个很小的比例，比如14%、15%的人实际上表示他们在接种疫苗后感觉更糟了。

sentences.en: So again, highly variable and still an awful lot we don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以再次说明，这变量极大，而且仍有大量我们未知的信息。

sentences.en: But at this point, Pam, in the pandemic and in our conversation, I think we'll take any measure of good news, of optimism, of not bad.
sentences.zh: 但帕姆，在大流行的这个阶段，在我们对话的这个时刻，我想我们愿意接受任何形式的好消息、乐观情绪或“情况不算太糟”的消息。

sentences.en: So thank you for that.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你分享这些。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金（Andrew Ross Sorkin）。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的

sentences.zh: DealBook

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订户，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不想错过。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 那么帕姆，这一切意味着什么？

sentences.en: So Pam, what are the implications of all this?
sentences.zh: 因为我们在讨论庞大群体中出现的一组非常严重的症状。

sentences.en: Because we're talking about a set of very serious symptoms across a very large population.
sentences.zh: 而且我们正处于大流行的一个时期，通过同事们的报道，我们现在意识到许多人感染COVID将不止一次，

sentences.en: And we're in a moment in the pandemic when we're now realizing, because of the reporting of our colleagues, that many people will not get COVID just once,
sentences.zh: 而是可能会多次感染COVID。

sentences.en: but perhaps get COVID multiple times.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们把所有这些结合起来思考时，这一切到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: So when we think about all that put together, what are the implications of all this?
sentences.zh: 我认为其影响将是极其深远的。

sentences.en: I think the implications will be very far-reaching.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们显然会影响到个体患者。

sentences.en: I think they are going to obviously affect individual patients.
sentences.zh: 它将影响社会以及社会的各个机构。

sentences.en: It will affect society and all the institutions of society.
sentences.zh: 并且它将影响医学本身以及医疗护理的提供方式。

sentences.en: And it will affect medicine itself and the way medical care is delivered.
sentences.zh: 让我们从个人开始。

sentences.en: Let's start with individuals.
sentences.zh: 你如何开始思考长新冠对受其折磨的个人的影响？

sentences.en: How do you start to think about the implications for individual people suffering from long COVID?
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，我认为我之前描述的那位34岁女性萨曼莎（Samantha）就是一个很好的典型例子。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I think the 34-year-old woman that I described earlier, Samantha, is a really good case in point.
sentences.zh: 她有一段时间不得不削减工作量。

sentences.en: She had to cut back on her job for a while.
sentences.zh: 她花了几个月的时间四处求医，包括去看了一位神经科医生，对方基本上让她“再加把劲”。

sentences.en: She spent several months going around to different doctors, including a neurologist who basically told her to try harder.
sentences.zh: 当她在大约最初感染后五六个月终于排到长新冠门诊的候诊名单时，

sentences.en: And when she finally got off the wait list for a post-COVID clinic about five or six months after she had originally gotten infected,
sentences.zh: 她接受了神经科医生的测试，其认知测试结果将她归入了几乎接近痴呆的类别。

sentences.en: she was tested by neurologists and her cognitive testing put her in a category of almost kind of a pre-dementia category.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 她得以参加一个名为“认知康复”（Cognitive Rehab）的项目，这种项目过去一直用于中风、

sentences.en: And she was able to enter a program that's called Cognitive Rehab, which is a kind of program that has been used for people
sentences.zh: 脑损伤或脑震荡等情况的患者。

sentences.en: who have strokes or brain injuries or concussions, things like that.
sentences.zh: 因此我跟随她进行了一周多次的物理治疗、职业治疗、记忆治疗。

sentences.en: And so I followed her for several times a week to physical therapy, occupational therapy, memory therapy.
sentences.zh: 她非常专注且极具决心。

sentences.en: And she was very dedicated and very determined.
sentences.zh: 这最终确实帮助她恢复到了某种功能水平，她现在状况有所好转，但并没有完全康复。

sentences.en: And it did end up helping her get back to a level of function where she is better now, but she's not completely better.
sentences.zh: 她的生活以及她正常运转所需的工具都发生了彻底的转变。

sentences.en: And her life and sort of the tools that she needs to function have completely shifted.
sentences.zh: 所以她把每件事都列成清单。

sentences.en: So she makes lists of everything.
sentences.zh: 她到处贴着便签，好让自己能记住去做事情。

sentences.en: She has note cards everywhere just so that she can remember to do things.
sentences.zh: 而最让我感到震惊的一件事是，我能够去拜访她并花了很多时间与她相处。

sentences.en: And And one of the things that was just so striking to me was I was able to, you know, visit her and spend a lot of time with her.
sentences.zh: 在她的浴室里，浴室镜子上贴着一张亮紫红色的索引卡，颜色鲜艳得让她绝不可能忽视。

sentences.en: And in her bathroom, posted on the bathroom mirror is a bright fuchsia index card, so bright that she couldn't possibly miss it.
sentences.zh: 上面歪歪扭扭地写着刷牙和用牙线所需的九个步骤，这样她就能记住顺序。

sentences.en: And on it, she's scrawled the nine steps that are required to brush and floss her teeth so that she can remember the order.
sentences.zh: 她是在2020年10月感染的。

sentences.en: And she was infected in October 2020.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在说的是一年半多的时间了，而她仍然在使用那张索引卡。
